description:

We are looking for a detail-oriented Data Cleansing Administrator to join our client's People Chief Operating Office team, supporting an important data archiving and decommissioning project.

- Confidence following established processes, written guidance and data handling procedures.
- Ability to maintain accurate records, document decisions and support audit requirements.
- Good written and verbal communication skills, with confidence escalating issues when necessary.
- Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Willingness to learn new systems, tools and processes quickly.
- Previous experience in data cleansing, data migration, records management or information governance would be advantageous.
- An understanding of data protection, confidentiality and records retention requirements would be beneficial.
- Experience supporting project delivery, data reconciliation, testing or UAT would be desirable.

Next steps

title: Train Planner
description:
Train Planner Swindon £25,500 £34,328 Permanent The Opportunity

If you're looking for an opportunity to play a key role in a growing rail operation while helping shape a newly established planning function, this is the kind of position that offers genuine influence from day one.

As part of a new regional Service Delivery Centre, you'll join a team responsible for planning and coordinating freight operations across the South region. Bringing together planning, control, and rostering activities under one roof, the new operation is designed to deliver faster decision-making, greater operational oversight, and improved service performance.

This is more than a traditional planning role. You'll help build the foundation that supports safe, efficient, and reliable freight services while contributing to the development of new processes and ways of working as the function evolves.

You'll be part of a newly created operation where planning processes, standards, and best practice are still being established, giving you the opportunity to influence how the function develops from the outset. At the same time, you'll gain specialist rail planning expertise within a business investing in growth, operational excellence, and long-term capability.

Whether you have existing rail planning experience or a transferable background in aviation, logistics, manufacturing, transport, or another scheduling-intensive environment, this role offers an excellent opportunity to build a rewarding career within freight operations.

Train Planner Responsibilities

Train Planning: Developing safe, compliant, and efficient operational plans that support the successful delivery of freight services across the South region.

Timetabling & Pathing: Constructing workable train paths and schedules that balance customer requirements, network capacity, operational resources, and service commitments.

Engineering Integration: Accounting for possessions, engineering works, access restrictions, and network constraints to ensure plans remain achievable and compliant.

Operational Coordination: Working closely with Control, Rostering, depots, and operational teams to ensure services are planned realistically and can be delivered reliably on the day.

Plan Validation & Compliance: Reviewing and validating plans to ensure accuracy, operational robustness, and adherence to industry and business requirements.

Ideal Train Planner

Scheduling & Planning Experience: Experience producing structured schedules, timetables, route plans, or operational programmes within a complex environment.

Constraint-Based Planning: Exposure to planning within resource limitations, engineering restrictions, access windows, or other operational constraints.

Sequencing & Problem Solving: Ability to resolve timing conflicts, prioritise competing demands, and develop practical, deliverable plans.

Stakeholder Collaboration: Experience working with operational, depot, resource, or delivery teams to coordinate planning activities effectively.

Compliance Awareness: Understanding of structured, regulated, or safety-critical environments where accuracy and adherence to procedures are essential.

Transferable Industry Experience: Relevant backgrounds may include rail, aviation scheduling, logistics planning, bus or tram timetabling, manufacturing production planning, or port and terminal operations.

Location & Working Arrangements

Location: Swindon

Working Pattern: Monday-Friday office-based with flexible start and finish times.

Train Planner Salary

Training Salary: £25,500

Qualified Salary: £34,328

title: Inventory and Procurement Coordinator
salary_text: £26000 - £30000 per year (free parking, pension, ongoing devel)
description:
Are you looking for a varied, hands-on role combining purchasing, stock control and supply chain coordination? Do you want to work for a company that truly focuses on the ongoing development of their staff?

Personnel Selection are looking for an Inventory & Purchasing Coordinator to join a growing team at our clients Salisbury offices.

Benefits include 23 days holiday + bank holidays, free parking, pension, company events and a real focus on your career development!

As our clients business continues to grow, they want to strengthen the purchasing and inventory functions, and this role will be central to making that happen.

The role will cover two key areas:

Purchasing & Supplier Coordination
- Raising and managing purchase orders, ensuring requirements are ordered accurately and on time.
- Liaising with suppliers to obtain order acknowledgements, confirm delivery dates and chase overdue orders.
- Monitoring supplier performance and escalating delivery or service issues.
- Checking supplier invoices and investigating any pricing or quantity discrepancies.
- Managing day-to-day requirements for consumables, workwear and mobile phones.
- Coordinating external services, including powder coating and waste collections.
- Building positive working relationships with suppliers and supporting general purchasing and supply chain activities.

Inventory Control & Warehouse Support
- Taking ownership of weekly stock counts and helping maintain accurate inventory records.
- Investigating stock discrepancies, shortages and booking-in issues, identifying root causes and helping prevent repeat problems.
- Supporting Goods In with part identification, checking deliveries and processing stock transactions.
- Maintaining accurate stock records and ensuring material traceability.
- Working closely with production to ensure materials are available when and where they are needed.
- Providing practical support within the warehouse when required, helping maintain an organised and efficient working environment.

We are not necessarily looking for someone with years of purchasing experience. We are more interested in finding the right person with a good attitude, strong organisational skills and the desire to develop.

Ideally, you will have experience in one or more of the following areas:
- Purchasing or procurement administration.
- Stock control or inventory management.
- Warehouse administration or Goods In.
- Supply chain or operations support.

Most importantly, you will be someone who doesn't mind rolling up their sleeves and getting stuck in!

This is a great opportunity to develop a broader understanding of purchasing, inventory management and the supply chain within a growing manufacturing business.

You will have the opportunity to make a genuine difference, helping improve stock accuracy, supplier performance and material availability while developing your own experience and capabilities.

We are looking for someone who wants to become a valued and reliable member of the team, take ownership of their responsibilities and grow with the business.

If you enjoy variety, like solving problems and want a role where your contribution genuinely matters, we would love to hear from you.

title: Recovery Coordinator
description:
Overview

Change Grow Live are a charity dedicated to the belief that we can make a difference to our Service Users lives, offering support and respect in a safe environment, treating each user as an individual and working with them to find the right treatment and care options.

Our core values are 'Be open, be compassionate and be bold' and our team members apply these daily to achieve our mission of helping people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals, and live life to its full potential.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Recovery Coordinator who has the skills and experience to assess and engage with our service users, ensuring that they access the right intervention at the right time, in a way that best meets their needs.

No two days are the same and we treat every person who comes into our service as an individual, so being flexible, curious and a good listener are key.

Where: HMP Erlestoke

Hours: 37.5 hours a week

Contract Type: Permanent

Full-time hours at Change Grow Live are 37.5 hours per week. For part-time roles, the salary and payments will be pro rata based on contracted hours.

Responsibilities

About the role:
- Supporting service users from point of entry into the service and through their treatment/recovery journey
- Providing screening, assessment, and recovery planning and onward referral
- Reducing drug and alcohol related harm to service users and the wider community
- Promoting carer, service user and community involvement
- Providing advocacy for access to partnership services
- Working with service users to support social (re)integration, enabling them to lead meaningful and purposeful lives: promoting recovery, resilience, peer support and self-determination
- Research, design and prepare subject matter and materials for groups / pods.
- Deliver structured content within group settings to service users at various stages of recovery
- Engage with debriefing and evaluations with co-facilitators after groups/pods have taken place, reviewing progress and identifying concerns with service users
- Tailor specific workshops around the needs of the service users, such as: anger management, sleep disorders, relationships, etc

About you:
- Have a strong understanding of substance misuse issues and experience of working within a similar field
- Experience of working with groups/pods and managing group dynamics, such as conflict or challenging behaviour.
- Be an excellent communicator, both verbal and written with good IT skills
- Proactive and able to work on own initiative with excellent time management and prioritising skills
- Have a good working knowledge of mental health interventions, services, and good practice
- Be a supportive team player with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work in partnership with a wide range of professionals, agencies, and internal/external stakeholders
- Ability to manage change successfully in a way that prioritises the needs of service users
- Understand the importance of information governance processes and commit to follow and apply all necessary safeguards
- Seek out learning opportunities to improve and broaden your professional knowledge and skills and to contribute and oversee the learning and development of others

What we will give to you:
- 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays. Additionally, you'll receive one extra day of annual leave for each year of service during your first five years, therefore you will enjoy 30 days of leave after five years with us.
- Paid 'Wellness' hour each week along with a 'Wellness' hub and Employee Assist Programme
- Contributory pension scheme
- Several benefits incl. discounts for shopping, cinema, holidays, etc.
- A friendly and supportive team
- Training, career development & progression opportunities
- Generous Refer-a-Friend Scheme

Please ensure that when completing your application form and supporting statement, you reflect on the details outlined in the job description. This will help us understand how your skills and experiences align with the requirements of the role.

AI can be a really helpful tool when putting together your application, and we're happy for you to use it. However, what we're most interested in is you.

We want to understand your experiences, achievements and strengths, so please make sure your application reflects your own story and clearly shows how you meet the essential criteria and the impact you've made in previous roles.

There's no need to write in a particular style. The strongest applications are those that are authentic, specific and clearly demonstrate your skills, experience and potential. We look forward to learning more about you.

Direct applications only - we will not be engaging agencies for this vacancy.

Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK at the time of application. For applicants with time-limited visas, unfortunately, we are unable to support new visa applications or extensions.

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high number of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
